blind_notes: Every key matched the reviewer's own answer. Rechecked against the official text: every RBR-4 Schedule I band edge and bandwidth (BND-003..009: 30 kHz, 20 kHz, 6 kHz, 1 kHz, 12 MHz, 26 dB, 430-450 MHz), C11 220-222 MHz disaster relief, C21 60 m 100 W PEP ERP / 2.8 kHz, s 10 power limits (250 W DC input, 560 W PEP, 190 W carrier, 3 dB amplifier margin), s 9 identification (30 min, English or French; US licensees 'mobile'/'portable' plus Schedule V prefix), s 3.2 foreign amateurs = Basic and Advanced, s 11 technical rules (29.5 MHz retransmission, 100% AM, crystal stability below 148 MHz, overmodulation indicator), s 13 30-day address change, Schedule V prefixes; Radiocommunication Regulations ss 15.3, 44, 46 (supervision and presence), 47, 48, 49, 52 and the amateur service definition; RIC-3 4.3, 4.4, 4.5.1 (kits, software reprogramming, repeater not remote control), 8.2 (CEPT and IARP by RAC, IARP Class 2 above 30 MHz); RIC-9 1.2 and 1.4.4 (new prefix on moving, one year for family). Every block-diagram item (STN-001..021, PSU-001/002) matches ISED's May 2025 labelled training diagrams (CW: oscillator, buffer driver, keyed power amplifier, filter; AM: VFO, buffer driver, modulator; FM: modulator, oscillator, frequency multiplier; HF: optional linear amplifier, LPF, SWR meter, tuner, switch). Every calculation recomputed: 24/300=80 mA, 0.25x56=14 V, 15/0.06=250 ohm, 810, 280, 80 ohm, 13.5 W, 4 A, 0.04x330=13.2 W, 1/2 ms=500 Hz, 10log4=6.0 dB, 200 W-10 dB=20 W, 120/5=24 V, 100 pF, 690 pF, image 100+2x10.7=121.4 MHz, 6x1.2=7.2 V, 20/4=5 h, 10log10=10 dB, 330 ohm, 680 kohm, 300/432=0.694 m, 300/160=1.875 MHz, 142/7.1=20.0 m, 71/14.2=5.0 m, 306/28.5=10.74 m, 2x50.125=100.25 MHz. No wrong key, no factual or outdated item found. Information only: in ID order the keys rotate strictly A, B, C, D; harmless because options are shuffled on every showing, but a re-shuffle at build time would be cleaner.

findings.issue: Surface cue: three distractors end in 'only' (RBR-4 standard only, ITU Radio Regulations only, RIC-3 circular only), so the one option without 'only' is the key. Options-only S hit.
findings.fix: Make the distractors parallel without 'only', e.g. 'Radiocommunication Act' vs 'Broadcasting Act', 'Telecommunications Act', 'Criminal Code' (check none of these also covers false distress before using it), or ask which section/document a candidate studies, not a law-status trap.

findings.issue: Options-only S hit: the three distractors (radiates its harmonics, gain exceeds 10 dBi, feed line is lossless) are false on their face, leaving the key by elimination.
findings.fix: Use plausible antenna-spec distractors, e.g. 'its front-to-back ratio stays above 15 dB', 'its gain stays within 3 dB of maximum', 'its feed-point impedance stays at exactly 50 ohms'.

findings.issue: Options-only S hit: the key restates the well-known secondary-service rule and the distractors (power below 100 W, FM only, register each station) read as invented.
findings.fix: Swap in distractors drawn from other Schedule I notes (e.g. 'use them only in disaster relief' (C11), 'keep to 100 W PEP ERP' (C21), 'need the Advanced Qualification').

findings.issue: Options-only S hit: 'Low-pass filter at the transmitter' is the only option whose filter type and place both fit; 'band-reject filter on the mains' is a strawman.
findings.fix: Use parallel distractors in the same form: 'High-pass filter at the transmitter', 'Low-pass filter at each receiver', 'Band-pass filter at each receiver'.

findings.issue: Options-only S hit (hard hat, insulated gloves, steel-toed boots vs safety harness: the only fall-related option). Also builder-flagged practice item; an official Canadian source exists: CCOHS on full-body harnesses (CSA Z259.10) and OHS legislation naming tower climbing as needing fall protection.
findings.fix: Keep the fact; replace distractors with other fall-protection items (body belt, positioning lanyard alone, rope tied round the waist) and cite CCOHS in sources.md.

findings.issue: Options-only S hit (the key is the only standard location). Builder-flagged: no free official source. The rule is Canadian Electrical Code Part I (CSA C22.1) Rules 54-200/54-202 and 54-800/54-802 (protector near the point of entry), which is paywalled; only a secondary guide was readable.
findings.fix: No official source readable: replace, or cite CSA C22.1 Section 54 by rule number if a copy can be read. If kept, write the explanation as 'near where the lead-in enters the building' to match the code wording.

findings.issue: Builder-flagged practice item (RST). No ISED or Canadian official definition found; RIC-3 topic 2-6 only names the RST system. The definition is published by ARRL (US national association), which originated it.
findings.fix: Keep; cite ARRL FSD-220 / Quick Reference Operating Aids in sources.md as the national-body source (no Canadian official source).

findings.issue: Same as OPS-010: tone figure only for CW is from ARRL operating aids, not an official Canadian page.
Builder-flagged courtesy item; now sourced: RAC's Recommended Repeater Operating Procedures says to monitor (listen) and determine whether the repeater is in use first.
findings.fix: Add the RAC page to sources.md.

findings.issue: Key sourced by RAC ('pause between transmissions to allow other Amateurs to identify themselves'), but the explanation's claim that 'break break is kept for urgent or emergency traffic' is not on the RAC page or any official source found.
findings.fix: Cite RAC; drop or soften the 'break break' sentence in the explanation.

findings.issue: No official source: CQ followed by your call sign phonetically is standard practice; ITU-R M.1172 defines CQ only, ITU RR Appendix 14 the phonetics, but no official document sets the voice CQ procedure.
findings.fix: No official source: replace, or keep only with a national-body source (RAC/ARRL operating guide) named in sources.md.

findings.issue: No official source for 'check the frequency is clear before tuning up'. RIC-3 topic 2-4 names 'tuneups and testing, use of dummy load, courteous operation' without text; RBR-4 s 11 only limits unmodulated carriers below 30 MHz to brief tests.
findings.fix: Replace with an item built on RBR-4 s 11 (unmodulated carrier below 30 MHz only for brief tests) or a dummy-load item, which have an official basis.

findings.issue: Builder-flagged (fuse protects the wiring). Partial official support: CCOHS says an oversized fuse can cause excessive current in the wiring and start a fire. CEC Rule 14-104 (paywalled) is the primary rule.

Builder-flagged (current across the chest most dangerous). Partial official support: CCOHS welding electrical safety page gives effects of current through the chest (fibrillation threshold) and says route determines severity.
Bonding cases so a fault trips protection: physics is sound; CCOHS only says tools should be grounded, CEC bonding rules (Section 10) are paywalled.

landing_findings.issue: FAQ says Basic lets you 'build station equipment from commercial kits'. RIC-3 4.5.1: Basic may build and operate all station equipment except home-made transmitters; only transmitters are limited to professional commercial kits. Understates the privilege.
landing_findings.fix: 'build any station equipment except transmitters, which must be assembled from commercial kits of professional design'.

landing_findings.issue: Info only, no change needed: RIC-3 5.4 still says no reference material and no memory calculators; the landing and examFacts follow the newer RIC-1 Issue 8 (formula sheet allowed, calculators that cannot store formulas or text). Format (100 questions, one per topic), 70% pass, 80% Honours, no time limit with most finishing within an hour, videoconference, no age or nationality limit, July 15 2025 bank update, Basic above 30 MHz at 250 W DC input: all confirmed on ISED pages.
